 "content": "# Continual-ARC periodic pattern notes

## Diagonal encodings
When sparse marks form parallel down-right diagonals, use the invariant `d = row - col` (0-indexed). The diagonals provide samples of a repeating 1D sequence indexed by `d`; extend the sequence across the grid using `d mod period`, after inferring the period and phase from marked diagonals. Validate all marks against the candidate rule before submitting.

- Solved `task-9945155d`: 18x18 had color 5 at d=5 and color 6 at d=10. Output is a checkerboard: 6 when `(row+col)%2 == 0`, else 5. (Equivalent d-parity mapping anchored by those marks.)
- Solved `task-b6a95784`: 27x27 had color 5 at d=-6, color 1 at d=-16 and d=7. These three samples establish period 3: `d mod 3 = 0 -> 5`, `1 -> 1`, `2 -> 1`. Fill every cell by that rule. For example, first row is `5,1,1,5,1,1,...`.

## Other periodic encodings seen in demos
Sparse horizontal full-width color rows can encode a repeating sequence of row colors: extend the sampled color sequence vertically. Examples showed different sequence periods and background colors, so infer period/phase from the actual anchors rather than assume a fixed period. Sparse diagonal motifs can also encode fully repeating 2D tiles; infer orientation and periodicity from the samples."
